quran.note: The angels give Maryam news of a word from Allah, “the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary”; his signs; “Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.”
Maryam withdraws; the Angel is sent; Isa is born; she is driven to the trunk of a palm tree.
Her people accuse her; she points to the child, who says, “Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.”
Allah says He will take him and raise him to Himself and purify him from those who disbelieve.
The example of Isa to Allah is like that of Adam: created from dust, then “Be”, and he was.
They did not kill him or crucify him; another was made to resemble him; Allah raised him to Himself; and before his death every one of the People of the Scripture will believe in him.
The Messiah was but a messenger of Allah and His word; do not say “three”; he would never disdain to be a servant of Allah.
Allah recalls His favour on Isa and his mother; the clay bird, healing and raising the dead by Allah’s permission; the disciples.
On the Day, Allah asks whether he told people to take him and his mother as deities; his answer.
He will be a sign for knowledge of the Hour.
Isa tells the Children of Israel he is Allah’s messenger confirming the Torah and giving good news of a messenger whose name is Ahmad.

hadith.summary: The Prophet ﷺ said he is the closest of all people to Isa, son of Maryam, in this world and the next, and that the prophets are like brothers from one father by different mothers: their religion is one.

The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah alone, that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, that Isa is Allah’s servant, His messenger and His word, and that Paradise and Hell are true, Allah will admit him to Paradise whatever his deeds. A narrator adds that Ubada said he may enter by whichever of its eight gates he wishes.
Umar reported the Prophet ﷺ warning people not to praise him beyond measure as the Christians praised Isa, son of Maryam: he is only a servant, so call him Allah’s servant and messenger.

hadith.narrator: Abu Huraira, through Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib
hadith.summary: The Prophet ﷺ said Satan touches every child at birth and the child cries out because of it, except Maryam and her son. Abu Huraira then recited the verse that asks Allah’s protection for Maryam and her offspring from the accursed Satan.
The Prophet ﷺ said Isa saw a man stealing and asked if he had stolen. The man swore by Allah that he had not, and Isa said he believed in Allah and did not trust his own eyes.

The Prophet ﷺ said only three spoke in infancy: Isa, son of Maryam; the infant in the story of the worshipper Jurayj; and a suckling baby who prayed not to be like a proud rider. The report tells the last two at length and does not record what Isa said.

The Prophet ﷺ said the Hour will not come until the son of Maryam descends among the people as a just judge and ruler: he will break the crosses, kill the swine and abolish the jizya, and wealth will be so abundant that no one will accept it as charity.
The long report on the Dajjal, the descent of Isa, and the release and destruction of Gog and Magog before the Last Hour.
In the Prophet’s ﷺ account of the night journey, Isa and Yahya are the prophets in the second heaven; they welcomed him as a brother and a prophet.
In the night-journey report, Isa and Yahya are met in the second heaven and are described as cousins on their mothers’ side.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: Gives an account, attributed to Ibn Abbas and recorded by Ibn Abi Hatim and by al-Nasa’i, in which Allah made a young man who volunteered look like Isa while Isa ascended from a hole in the roof; the man was seized and crucified. Ibn Kathir says this report has an authentic chain to Ibn Abbas and that many of the Salaf said Isa asked for a volunteer. He adds that the Jews who claimed to have killed Isa, and the Christians who believed them, are in doubt and follow only conjecture. This is explanation, not revelation: the Qur’an says only that “another was made to resemble him”.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: On “before his death”: concludes that it refers to the death of Isa, son of Maryam. It records Ibn Abbas to that effect and Abu Malik that the belief of the People of the Scripture comes after Isa returns and before he dies. It cites the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the descent in al-Bukhari and Muslim, and notes that Abu Hurayrah recited this verse after it; a narrator in one version was unsure whether that addition was part of the Prophet’s ﷺ words or Abu Hurayrah’s own.
